title: Greeting to the Church in Tralles
english: Ignatius, who is also called God-Bearer, to the holy church in Tralles of Asia, beloved by God the Father of Jesus Christ, chosen and worthy of God, at peace in flesh and spirit through the passion of Jesus Christ, who is our hope in the resurrection to him. I greet her in the fullness, in apostolic character, and I pray that she may rejoice greatly.
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Tralles with a formal greeting, identifying himself and blessing the church.

title: Ignatius praises the Trallians' blameless mind and Polybius's visit
english: I have come to know that you have a blameless and undivided mind in endurance, not by practice but by nature, as Polybius your bishop made clear to me. He came to Smyrna by the will of God and Jesus Christ, and he rejoiced with me, bound as I am in Christ Jesus, so much that I saw your whole multitude in him.
So I received through him your godly goodwill, and I gave glory, finding you, as I have learned, to be imitators of God.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Tralles while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he praises their blameless mind and the visit of their bishop Polybius.

title: Submission to bishop, elders, and deacons
english: When you submit to the bishop as you would to Jesus Christ, it is clear to me that you are not living in a merely human way. You are living according to Jesus Christ, who died for us so that by believing in his death you might escape death itself.

So it is necessary, as you are already doing, that you do nothing without the bishop. Submit also to the council of elders as you would to the apostles of Jesus Christ our hope, in whom we will be found if we live in him.

The deacons, since they serve the mysteries of Jesus Christ, must please everyone in every way. They are not deacons of food and drink, but servants of the church of God. They must therefore guard themselves against accusations as they would guard against fire.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, urging them to live in unity under their bishop, council of elders, and deacons.

title: Honor deacons, elders, and bishop as God's order
english: In the same way, let everyone respect the deacons as they would Jesus Christ, just as they should also respect the bishop, who is a pattern of the Father, and the council of elders as the council of God and as a bond of the apostles. Without these, a church is not called a church.

I am persuaded that you already hold this view. For I received the pattern of your love and I have it with me in your bishop, whose very disposition is a great discipleship and whose gentleness is power. I consider that even the godless respect him.
Because I love you, I am sparing you, though I could write more sharply about this matter. I did not think that, being condemned, I should give you orders as if I were an apostle.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, urging them to honor their deacons, elders, and bishop as the visible order of God.

title: Fear of boasting and the need for gentleness
english: I have many thoughts in God, but I take my own measure, so that I do not perish through boasting. For now I must be more afraid, and not pay attention to those who puff me up. For those who speak to me whip me.

I do love the suffering, but I do not know whether I am worthy. For zeal is not visible to many, but it wars against me all the more. So I need gentleness, in which the ruler of this age is destroyed.
orientation: Ignatius, bishop of Antioch, is writing to the church in Tralles while being taken under guard to Rome, and here he reflects on his own spiritual state and the danger of pride.

title: Heavenly knowledge and the limits of discipleship
english: Can I not write to you about heavenly things? I am afraid to, because you are still infants. I fear I would set before you something harmful. Forgive me: perhaps you could not take it in, and you would choke on it.

For even I, though I am in chains and can understand heavenly things, the ranks of the angels and the assemblies of the rulers, visible and invisible, am not yet a disciple for that reason. For we still lack much if we are not to fall short of God.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, explaining why he withholds deeper heavenly teaching from them and reflecting on his own unworthiness as a disciple.

title: Only Christian food, not the poison of false teaching
english: So I urge you, not I myself but the love of Jesus Christ: take only Christian food, and keep away from any foreign plant, which is false teaching.

These people weave Jesus Christ into themselves while claiming to be worthy of trust, like those who give a deadly poison mixed with honeyed wine. The one who does not know takes it gladly, with evil pleasure, and so receives death.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Trallians against false teachers who mix Christ with error, after saying he could not safely teach them heavenly things.

title: Guard against false teachers by staying within the altar
english: So guard yourselves against such people. You will be able to do this if you are not puffed up and if you remain inseparable from God Jesus Christ, from the bishop, and from the ordinances of the apostles.

The one who is inside the altar is clean, but the one who is outside the altar is not clean. That is, anyone who does anything apart from the bishop, the council of elders, and the deacons is not clean in conscience.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Trallians against false teachers, telling them that purity comes from remaining within the church's order under the bishop.

title: Guard against the devil's ambushes
english: It is not that I have found anything like this among you. But I am guarding you in advance, because you are dear to me, foreseeing the ambushes of the devil. So take up gentleness and regain yourselves in faith, which is the flesh of the Lord, and in love, which is the blood of Jesus Christ.

Let none of you hold anything against a neighbor. Do not give the nations occasion to blaspheme, so that the multitude in God may not be blasphemed because of a few foolish people. For woe to the one through whom God's name is blasphemed among some on account of vanity.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, warning them to protect themselves against the devil's schemes.

title: The True Birth, Death, and Resurrection of Jesus
english: So make yourselves deaf whenever anyone speaks to you apart from Jesus Christ. He was of the family of David and of Mary. He truly was born, and he ate and drank. He truly was persecuted under Pontius Pilate, truly was crucified and died, while the heavenly, earthly, and subterranean beings were watching.
He also truly was raised from the dead. His Father raised him. According to this pattern, his Father will also raise us who believe in him, in Christ Jesus. Apart from him we do not have true life.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Trallians against false teachers, and here he states the real events of Jesus's life as the ground of Christian faith.

title: If Christ only seemed to suffer, Ignatius's chains and death are meaningless
english: But if, as some godless people—that is, faithless people—say, he suffered in mere appearance, then they themselves are mere appearance. Why am I bound? Why do I pray for martyrdom by beasts? Then I am dying in vain. Am I then lying about the Lord?
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, arguing against teachers who say Christ only seemed to suffer, and he is contrasting their claim with the reality of his own imprisonment and coming martyrdom.

title: Flee the deadly offshoots; be branches of the cross
english: So flee from these evil offshoots that produce death-bringing fruit. If anyone tastes it, he dies on the spot. These people are not a planting of the Father. If they were, they would show themselves as branches of the cross, and their fruit would be imperishable. Through the cross, in his passion, he calls you, who are his members. A head cannot come to be without members, since God promises unity, and that unity is himself.
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Trallians against teachers who deny the real suffering of Christ, and now tells them to flee these false teachers because they are not God's planting.

title: Greetings, bonds, and a plea for unity from Smyrna
english: I greet you from Smyrna, together with the churches of God that are here with me. They have refreshed me in every way, both in flesh and in spirit.

My chains, which I carry around for the sake of Jesus Christ, exhort you, asking that you may attain God: remain in your concord and in prayer with one another. For it is fitting for each one of you, and especially the council of elders, to refresh the bishop for the honor of the Father, Jesus Christ, and the apostles.
I pray that you will listen to me in love, so that I may not be a witness among you by having written.
orientation: Ignatius, writing from Smyrna, closes his letter to the Trallians with greetings, a plea that they remain united in prayer, and a wish that his letter not become a witness against them.

title: Prayer, greetings, and final exhortation to unity
english: Pray for me too. I need the love that comes from you, through the mercy of God, so that I may be counted worthy of the lot that surrounds me and that I hope to obtain, and so that I may not be found unapproved.
The love of the Smyrnaeans and Ephesians greets you. Remember in your prayers the church in Syria. I am not worthy to be called from there, since I am the least of them.
Be strong in Jesus Christ. Submit to the bishop as to the commandment, and likewise to the council of elders. And love one another, each one of you, with an undivided heart.

My spirit purifies you, not only now but also when I attain God. For I am still under danger, but the Father is faithful in Jesus Christ to fulfill my request and yours. In him may you be found blameless.
orientation: Ignatius is closing his letter to the Trallians, asking for their prayers, sending greetings from Smyrna and Ephesus, and giving final commands about submission to the bishop and mutual love.
